slides.texte_overlay:
The morning routine that
makes you sharp by noon
Get daylight in the first 15 minutes. Open the curtains, step outside, walk to get coffee. Morning light wakes up your brain faster than any alarm.
Drink a big glass of water before coffee. You've been dry for eight hours. Hydrating first makes the coffee work better and clears the morning fog.
Leave your phone in another room for the first hour. No emails, no news, no feeds. Your best focus of the day shouldn't go to other people's noise.
Do your hardest task first. Before meetings, before messages. Ninety minutes of deep work in the morning beats a full afternoon of half-focused effort.
Warm up your brain. I do five minutes of history, art or science with breakfast, and my mind is awake and curious before the work day even starts.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app with breakfast. History, art, science. My mind is awake and curious before work even starts.

slides.texte_overlay: Eat protein, not just sugar. Eggs, yoghurt, nuts. A real breakfast keeps your energy steady all morning instead of crashing at eleven, right when you need focus most.
Take a 5-minute walk before lunch. Fresh air and movement reset your focus, so you finish the morning as sharp and focused as you started it, every day.
